messages:
maria_cs: Customer (ACME) opened a ticket — invoice shows ~3.2M tokens but dashboard shows ~2.1M. They claim heavy use of streaming chat and frequent client disconnects. Can someone triage?

devon_support: Filed ticket #C-9942 with request_id from customer: r-8f3b2a0. They provided a screenshot of the dashboard and the invoice PDF. Customer says they cancel streams often when they get the answer early.

ingrid_billing: Noted. Invoice numbers are computed from the billing pipeline (post-aggregation). Dashboards pull near-real-time counts from the usage index. There have been a few edge cases where streaming messages were reprocessed.

sre_jake: Can we get the raw request logs + runtime emission logs for that request_id? I want to check whether tokens were counted on generation completion or on emission.

maria_cs: Customer attached server-request logs and a minimal client repro. They said model=redwood-rlm-large-v2, streaming=true, protocol=SSE, client=browser fetch + EventSource polyfill, sometimes HTTP/2 via our LB.

eng_ana: Pasting the customer's SSE snippet they attached:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream

data: {"id":"r-8f3b2a0","object":"chunk","delta":{"content":"Hel"}}

data: {"id":"r-8f3b2a0","object":"chunk","delta":{"content":"lo "}}

data: {"id":"r-8f3b2a0","object":"chunk","delta":{"content":"world"}}

event: done
id: r-8f3b2a0

```

eng_ana: But the customer said their client triggers a cancel (EventSource close / XHR abort) mid-stream right after receiving first two chunks. They see their dashboard token usage lower than invoice. Hypothesis: when client cancels, some runtime paths still finish the generation; our billing pipeline may count tokens again when finalization/resume occurs.

sre_jake: Found runtime logs for r-8f3b2a0 in infra-prod-1:

```
[2024-03-12T14:07:02Z] req=r-8f3b2a0 state=stream_emit chunk_tokens=3 total_tokens_emitted=3
[2024-03-12T14:07:02Z] req=r-8f3b2a0 client_conn=closed code=499 reason="client aborted"
[2024-03-12T14:07:02Z] req=r-8f3b2a0 state=finish_generation gen_tokens=1024 billed_flag=queued
[2024-03-12T14:07:03Z] billing: enqueue r-8f3b2a0 tokens=1024
```

sre_jake: Looks like runtime continued a background generation after the connection closed and then enqueued the full gen_tokens to billing. Dashboard counts emission events (3 tokens emitted) while billing pipeline consumed the queued finalization (1024 tokens). That would explain the delta.

devon_support: Customer wants to know: who billed them for the extra tokens? Is that expected behavior?

ingrid_billing: Current documented behavior: we bill for tokens generated by the model, not strictly tokens sent over the wire. But product promised "tokens used" in dashboard – mismatch in user expectations. We need to make both consistent or at least show a note for streaming cancels.

eng_ana: Root cause summary for now: streaming cancel triggers connection close but the generation job isn't immediately cancelled in some runtime cases (race between LB connection tear-down and backend cancellation). If the runtime finishes and writes a finalization record, billing counts the generated tokens. Dashboards only index emitted chunks.

maria_cs: Proposed next steps? Customer asks for a remediation + credit if we were at fault.

eng_ana: Short-term mitigation: patch runtime to aggressively cancel model execution on client disconnect (PR #4721). Also change billing pipeline to dedupe tokens for requests that had partial emission + finalization within N seconds — mark as "stream-partial" and prefer emitted count if finalization occurred post-disconnect within 10s.

ingrid_billing: We should offer a one-time invoice adjustment for ACME while we deploy the fix. I'll prepare reversal for the 1.1M token delta pending SRE confirmation.

sre_jake: Repro steps for internal testing (copyable):

1) Start a server-side stream: curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
   "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-rlm-large-v2" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}],"stream":true}'
2) After receiving first two events, kill the client (Ctrl-C) or send FIN to LB.
3) Check runtime logs for req id and watch for background gen completion.

Also experiment with http2 vs http1.1 — LB path behaves differently and race window changes.

devon_support: Can we detect client aborts earlier? Any headers or socket events we can surf?

eng_ana: We already surface socket close events in the streaming handler but there are two tricky cases: (a) LB acknowledges but backend doesn't get immediate socket close (graceful drain), (b) long short-circuit retry logic where a worker transparently retries generation after a partial failure. Fix involves the runtime honoring the socket-close event with a hard cancel token to the model inference process.

maria_cs: I've messaged ACME that we're looking into root cause, offered a provisional credit, and requested permission to adjust invoice once SRE confirms. They replied :thumbsup:.

streaming-bot: New issue created: github.com/redwood/runtime/issues/512 — "cancel-propagation: ensure model exec cancels on connection close". Tagging eng_ana + sre_jake.

ingrid_billing: I'll hold the invoice autocharge until we confirm. If SRE confirms billing delta is internal, we'll issue credit and include a note on streaming billing semantics in docs.

sre_jake: I'll run the repro and attach logs to the ticket. If we confirm this repro on 3/13 deploy (can reproduce on prod-1 with LB variant B), plan: hotfix in runtime, then a billing pipeline dedupe change, with monitoring alert for requests where billed_tokens > emitted_tokens + 50%.

devon_support: Thanks team — I'll keep ACME updated and will escalate to TA if they push back.

maria_cs: Closing loop: once fixes merged, please post here with PR links and ETA so I can update the customer.

eng_ana: PRs: runtime#4721 (cancel propagation), billing#198 (dedupe stream finals), docs#211 (streaming billing doc). ETA: runtime hotfix in 48–72h, billing patch under next sprint.

maria_cs: Great, thx :raised_hands:
